_note: IFA knowledge base — seeded with Iwori Ofun (personal Odu) and the 16 Meji. Add entries incrementally. Specific ebo and akose should always be confirmed with lineage elders.

odu.name: Iwori Ofun
odu.personal_note: This is the user's personal Odu (Odu Ori). It receives priority treatment in all consultations.
themes: Hidden knowledge and secrets — the person carries deep wisdom that must be revealed at the right time
Exceptional intelligence and mental power — the mind is the greatest tool
Spiritual revelation — what was concealed will be uncovered
The tongue as both weapon and gift — words have enormous power here, for good and destruction
Transformation through crisis — challenges that seem catastrophic are often initiations
The danger of knowing too much and speaking too soon
Enemies who operate in shadow — not all opposition is visible
strengths: Natural intelligence and ability to see through deception
Power of persuasion when words are used correctly
Resilience — this Odu has survived and overcome
Strong connection to Orunmila and the wisdom of IFA
Natural authority — people follow this person
Ability to succeed in business through strategic thinking
warnings: Do not reveal secrets or confidential information at the wrong time
Guard against gossip — words spoken carelessly can destroy what took years to build
Watch for hidden enemies, especially among those who appear to be friends
Do not let intelligence become arrogance
Business partnerships require extreme caution — scrutinize contracts and intentions
Avoid making decisions in anger — the mind must be clear
Do not neglect Eshu/Elegba — all roads must be open
Pride in knowledge without humility leads to downfall
odu.ese_ifa_summary: In Iwori Ofun, the verses speak of a wise elder who possessed great knowledge but whose words, when spoken carelessly, brought ruin. After consulting IFA and performing the required ebo, the elder learned to speak only what was needed, at the moment it was needed — and became a source of healing rather than conflict. The Odu teaches that intelligence without discipline is a blade without a handle.

ebo.note: Specific ebo materials and procedures vary significantly by lineage (Nigerian vs. Afrocuban) and by the specific situation revealed in the divination. What follows is general guidance — consult your lineage for exact prescriptions.
general: Eshu/Elegba must always be propitiated first in this Odu — no other work proceeds without opening the roads
Oshun receives offerings for matters of love, money, and sweetening difficult situations
Ogun receives offerings when there are conflicts, legal matters, or obstacles that require cutting through
The mouth and tongue are often involved in ebo — words that were spoken wrongly may need to be corrected spiritually
White cloth and white foods (coconut, shea butter) appear frequently in prescriptions
Cold water and calm are emphasized — heat and anger are what this Odu cautions against

akose.note: Akose (spiritual medicines and preparations) in this Odu are lineage-specific and must be prepared by a trained babalawo. General categories are listed below.
remedies: Preparations for protection of the head (ori) — the mind is the seat of power in this Odu
Herbal baths for clarity and removal of confusion or spiritual fog
Work with plants associated with Oshun (such as cinnamon, honey, sunflowers) for drawing sweetness
Protective preparations against hidden enemies and spiritual attacks
Remedies for the voice and speech when words have caused damage that needs to be healed

odu.nigerian_tradition_notes: In traditional Nigerian IFA, Iwori Ofun is approached with a strong emphasis on the Ese IFA (poetry/verses) which contain the specific prescriptions. The babalawo recites the relevant verses and prescribes ebo based on what the Odu says in that sitting. Ogun and Eshu are given particular prominence in the Nigerian approach to this Odu.
odu.cuban_tradition_notes: In Afrocuban (Lucumi/Santería) tradition, this Odu is handled within the framework of Ifa initiation (Kofabori or Itefa depending on path). Ellegua (Eshu) is considered the most important Orisha to propitiate in this sign. Oshun's energy is strong here and her guidance is often sought. The specific letra (sign) governs what patakines (stories) are read and what rogaciones (head prayers) are prescribed.

odu.name: Ogbe Meji
themes: The first and senior Odu — father of all other signs
Direct connection to Obatala and purity
strengths: Divine favor when living with integrity
warnings: Pride is this Odu's greatest danger
Obatala's prohibitions must be respected strictly
Avoid alcohol and excess
Do not compromise integrity for short-term gain
odu.ese_ifa_summary: Ogbe Meji is the first light — it was present at creation. The verses speak of Orunmila descending to Earth and establishing IFA. This Odu carries divine authority but also the responsibility of living as an example.

ebo.note: Lineage-specific. Obatala is central to most prescriptions in this Odu.
general: Obatala receives white offerings — white cloth, coconut, shea butter, white pigeons
Purity of conduct is itself an ebo in Ogbe Meji
Ogun may need to be propitiated to clear obstacles

akose.note: Consult your lineage for specific preparations.
remedies: White herbal baths for purification and spiritual elevation
Head prayers and rogaciones with white materials

odu.nigerian_tradition_notes: Eji Ogbe is the greatest Odu in Nigerian IFA. It opens all divination sessions and its Ese IFA are the most extensive.
odu.cuban_tradition_notes: In Lucumi tradition, Ogbe Meji carries the same seniority. Obatala governs this sign completely.

odu.name: Oyeku Meji
themes: The transition between states of being
Ancestral connection and communication with the dead
What must end so something new can begin
strengths: Ability to navigate transformation and change
Spiritual authority in matters of life and death
Strong protective power when properly aligned
warnings: This Odu requires constant awareness of spiritual health
Neglecting the ancestors brings serious consequences
Ebo must not be delayed when this Odu appears
Guard against depression and stagnation
odu.ese_ifa_summary: Oyeku Meji teaches that death is not an end but a passage. Its verses speak of the necessity of completing cycles. What has served its purpose must be released for new life to come forward.

ebo.note: Lineage-specific. Ancestor veneration is always central.
general: Egun (ancestors) must be honored and fed before other work
Black and white materials appear frequently
Oya receives offerings when transition and transformation are needed

odu.nigerian_tradition_notes: In Nigerian IFA, Oyeku is understood as the night force that balances Ogbe (the day force). Together they hold creation in balance.
odu.cuban_tradition_notes: In Lucumi, this Odu is treated with great seriousness. Divination in Oyeku Meji often results in immediate ebo to address spiritual dangers.

odu.name: Iwori Meji
themes: The power of intention and thought
What the heart knows that the eyes cannot see
warnings: Heart must be guarded — vulnerability is both power and risk
Do not act from unchecked emotion
odu.ese_ifa_summary: Iwori Meji speaks of the heart as the seat of knowledge. The eyes see what is outside; the heart sees what is true.

general: Oshun is propitiated for heart matters
Eshu clears the path

odu.nigerian_tradition_notes: Iwori is the third of the 16 principal Odu.
odu.cuban_tradition_notes: In Lucumi, Iwori Meji emphasizes the role of intention in spiritual work.

odu.name: Odi Meji
strengths: Ability to bring hidden things to light
warnings: Secrets kept too long become poison
Avoid jealousy and hidden resentment
odu.ese_ifa_summary: Odi Meji speaks of the power that lives in hidden places — like a seed in the earth, transformation happens where the eye cannot see.

general: Oya governs transitions in this Odu

odu.cuban_tradition_notes: Strong Oya energy in Cuban tradition.

odu.name: Irosun Meji
warnings: Excess leads to destruction
Guard health — especially blood-related conditions
Emotions must not override judgment
odu.ese_ifa_summary: Irosun Meji teaches that pleasure and wealth are gifts that carry responsibility.

general: Oshun is central — honey, gold, yellow flowers
Shango for strength and justice

odu.nigerian_tradition_notes: Fifth principal Odu. Strong Oshun energy.
odu.cuban_tradition_notes: Known as Oshe Meji in Lucumi. Oshun governs almost entirely.

odu.name: Owonrin Meji
strengths: Ability to turn chaos into opportunity
warnings: Instability if not grounded
Impulsiveness leads to regret
Do not make sudden moves without consulting IFA
odu.ese_ifa_summary: Owonrin Meji is the Odu of the unexpected. It warns that what appears to be disorder is often divine reorganization.

general: Eshu must be constantly fed in this Odu
Stability work with Obatala

odu.nigerian_tradition_notes: Sixth principal Odu. Known for its complex and numerous Ese IFA.
odu.cuban_tradition_notes: Strong Ellegua presence. Unpredictability is honored rather than feared.

odu.name: Obara Meji
warnings: Pride is the poison of this Odu
Generosity must be genuine, not performance
Do not let ego override wisdom
odu.ese_ifa_summary: Obara Meji says: the true king is known by his generosity. Power that does not serve eventually destroys itself.

general: Shango receives offerings for strength and justice
Royal colors — red and white

odu.cuban_tradition_notes: Shango governs this sign in Lucumi. Royal protocol is emphasized.

odu.name: Okanran Meji
themes: The warrior who fights to protect
warnings: Aggression without direction destroys the self
Choose battles wisely
Hot head leads to cold regret
odu.ese_ifa_summary: Okanran Meji is the warrior's Odu. It does not avoid conflict — it teaches how to fight with purpose and when to sheathe the blade.

general: Ogun is central — iron, rum, cigars
Eshu clears the path before battle

odu.nigerian_tradition_notes: Eighth principal Odu. Ogun and conflict are central themes.
odu.cuban_tradition_notes: Ogun and Ellegua are both critical in this sign in Lucumi.

odu.name: Ogunda Meji
themes: The labor that builds lasting things
warnings: Do not work without rest — Ogun's children burn out
Avoid violence outside of protection
Stubbornness must not replace wisdom
odu.ese_ifa_summary: Ogunda Meji teaches that the path is cleared by those willing to work. Nothing stands before genuine effort aligned with Ogun's power.

general: Ogun is primary — iron tools, rum, palm oil
Hard physical labor can itself be ebo

odu.cuban_tradition_notes: Ogun dominates completely. Work and the forge are sacred.

odu.name: Osa Meji
warnings: Anger is this Odu's greatest danger
Uncontrolled emotions invite spiritual attack
Respect the feminine forces or face consequences
odu.ese_ifa_summary: Osa Meji speaks of the power that lives in women and the spiritual forces associated with them. The wise person honors this power; the foolish person dismisses it and suffers.

general: Oya and Yemoja receive offerings
The Aje are honored with specific protocols

odu.nigerian_tradition_notes: Tenth principal Odu. The Aje (feminine spiritual forces) are central.
odu.cuban_tradition_notes: Oya and Yemaya both feature strongly in this Odu in Lucumi.

odu.name: Ika Meji
themes: Rebellion and the refusal to conform
The outsider who carries important gifts
What society rejects that is actually sacred
Taboo and the laws broken with consequence
strengths: The ability to see what others refuse to see
Gifts that come precisely because of being different
warnings: Rebellion without purpose is self-destruction
Do not break taboos carelessly
Isolation chosen too often becomes a trap
odu.ese_ifa_summary: Ika Meji is the Odu of the one who walks a different road. Its verses speak of gifts hidden in rejection and the price paid for refusing to conform — but also the greater price of denying your nature.

general: Eshu/Elegba is essential for opening roads that others cannot access
Obatala for clarity of purpose

odu.cuban_tradition_notes: Strong Ellegua energy. The crossroads between worlds.

odu.name: Oturupon Meji
themes: What is owed and must be paid
strengths: Deep spiritual awareness of cause and consequence
The ability to pay debts and move forward cleanly
warnings: Ingratitude is fatal in this Odu
Do not forget those who helped you
Spiritual debts do not disappear — they collect interest
odu.ese_ifa_summary: Oturupon Meji warns of the spiritual law of reciprocity. The person who forgets where they came from will find themselves returned there.

general: Settling spiritual and material debts is itself ebo
Eshu governs what is owed

odu.cuban_tradition_notes: Debt and reciprocity are emphasized in Lucumi practice.

odu.name: Otura Meji
themes: Divine wisdom and the source of IFA itself
The covenant between humans and Orun (heaven)
strengths: Access to the deepest levels of IFA wisdom
Divine protection of the highest order when aligned
The capacity to teach and transmit sacred knowledge
warnings: Sacred responsibilities must not be neglected
Knowledge without action is waste
The covenant with Orunmila must be honored
odu.ese_ifa_summary: Otura Meji is Orunmila's own sign. Its verses carry the origin stories of IFA and the terms of the agreement between humans and the divine.

general: Orunmila is propitiated directly
White offerings for Obatala

odu.nigerian_tradition_notes: Thirteenth principal Odu. Considered Orunmila's personal sign.
odu.cuban_tradition_notes: Treated with highest reverence in Lucumi IFA.

odu.name: Irete Meji
themes: Wealth, abundance, and the earth's generosity
The farmer who works with nature
Patience as the path to prosperity
What the earth gives to those who tend it
strengths: Capacity for sustained effort that builds lasting wealth
Connection to natural and herbal medicine
warnings: Impatience destroys the harvest before it arrives
Do not take more than what is needed
Neglect of the earth (physical and spiritual) leads to famine
odu.ese_ifa_summary: Irete Meji speaks of the farmer who plants in faith and tends with care. The harvest does not come immediately, but it comes completely.

general: Orisha Oko receives agricultural offerings
Osanyin governs herbal work in this Odu

odu.nigerian_tradition_notes: Fourteenth principal Odu. Strong connection to herbal medicine (Osanyin).
odu.cuban_tradition_notes: Agricultural and herbal themes are preserved in Lucumi practice.

odu.name: Ose Meji
themes: The sacred and the profane united
What desire creates when channeled correctly
strengths: Creative and sexual power as a generative force
The ability to attract and magnetize
Strong capacity for legacy and creation
warnings: Uncontrolled desire becomes the person's destruction
Sexual energy must be channeled, not suppressed or indulged without boundaries
Guard against being manipulated through desire
odu.ese_ifa_summary: Ose Meji teaches that Oshun's gifts — beauty, love, pleasure — are sacred when honored and destructive when abused.

general: Oshun is central — honey, gold, river water
Shango for grounding sexual power in strength

odu.cuban_tradition_notes: Oshun dominates in Lucumi. Sensuality and beauty are honored as divine gifts.

odu.name: Ofun Meji
themes: Death, disease, and the ultimate transformation
What must die so life continues
The medicine that heals through crisis
strengths: The deepest capacity for healing — one who has faced darkness can heal darkness in others
Spiritual authority earned through suffering and transformation
warnings: This Odu requires constant spiritual maintenance — neglect here has serious consequences
Do not resist necessary endings
The body must be cared for with discipline
odu.ese_ifa_summary: Ofun Meji is the last of the 16 principal Odu and carries the weight of all that comes before it. Its verses speak of death not as enemy but as the final purification — the transformation that makes eternal things possible.

ebo.note: Lineage-specific. Ebo in this Odu is often urgent.
general: Obatala for purity and protection
Oya for transition
Egun (ancestors) must be honored and consulted

odu.nigerian_tradition_notes: Sixteenth and final principal Odu. Carries enormous spiritual weight.
odu.cuban_tradition_notes: In Lucumi, Ofun Meji is approached with great seriousness and care. Ebo is rarely optional when this Odu speaks.
